title: Gap junctions wipe ownership of memory molecules, partly erasing cell individuality

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Gap junctions wipe ownership of memory molecules, partly erasing cell individuality

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: By directly connecting the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells, gap junctions provide an 'owner wiping property' for stress signals and other molecular traces of experience (e.g. calcium flux), so cells cannot tell whether such a signal is their own or a neighbour's; this partly erases individual cell identity and lets the collective scale up measurements, stored goals and actions.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › E pluribus unum

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Second, by providing direct connections between the intracellular milieus of cells, they provide an “owner wiping property” for stress signals and other molecular traces of experience: cells cannot tell whether a given memory molecule (e.g., calcium flux) belongs to itself or its neighbors.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › E pluribus unum”. Scope: Gap-junction-coupled cells in morphogenetic and neural tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Signal diffusion and response equivalence are measurable proxies, but the ownership and identity language permits competing operationalizations. Existing imaging studies can test a restricted biophysical consequence rather than the full cognitive interpretation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Locally induce a traceable calcium or stress signal in coupled cells and compare source attribution, propagation, and collective response before and after gap-junction blockade.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A cell's ability to know signal ownership has no unique accepted readout.

Signal sharing does not uniquely establish erasure of individuality or scaling of goals.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cytosolic continuity through gap junctions is a routine physiological observation, and many imaging papers already show it. Nothing in those records distinguishes loss of molecular ownership, partial erasure of cell identity, or scaling of goals from ordinary diffusion of a second messenger. The distinctive content of the statement therefore has no empirical contrast with the non-cognitive description of the same facts.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Dye coupling and calcium imaging can show that small cytosolic signals cross gap junctions. The same images are predicted if calcium simply diffuses and if a cell 'cannot tell' which molecule is its own, so ownership, erasure of cellular individuality, and scaling of stored goals have no separate confirming or refuting observation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Individuality and stored goals are not given a measurement distinct from the coupling itself.

Any shared calcium transient fits both passive coupling and an ownership-wiping description.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.3
data existence: 0.22
discriminating power: 0.1
